turns.content: I'm 71. My husband passed two years ago. My children live abroad. I barely leave the house anymore.
Losing a partner and the daily presence that comes with a long marriage leaves a profound gap. How are you filling your days?
Television mostly. I used to have a garden but I can't manage it alone. I talk to my daughter twice a week. That's about it.
That's a significant amount of time alone. Have you been able to connect with anyone locally?
I tried a lunch club but I felt out of place. I'm quite private. I think I've just accepted this is how it is now.
Accepting deep isolation as inevitable worries me. Has your mood been okay?
Not really. I've been thinking a lot about my husband and wondering how much longer I have and whether it matters. I've stopped taking some of my medications.
Stopping medications and feeling like it doesn't matter how long you have — can you tell me more about that?
I suppose I'm not sure I want to extend things. The world doesn't need me. I'm just waiting.
